segments: The eleventh dynasty.
Hunnic (Mongol) Kings.
that they should not wrong anyone,
and if not, they should fear for their heads lest they be cut off.
In these days we heard
that the ruler of Egypt sent that Sheikh Abd al-Rahman and those who were with him from Damascus to the fortress of Safed,
and he imprisoned them there, so that hope of their release was cut off.
And in this year, 1506 of the Greeks (1195 AD):
a hen laid,
in the village of Bartelli,
an egg which was close in size to a goose egg.
And in the week of the Passion of our Savior,
another hen laid, in that same Bartelli, a small egg which had a neck that was thin, curved, and long, like that of a gourd.
And they brought it before us, and we saw it.
And on Sunday the twenty-ninth (29th) of Tammuz, in the morning,
a raiding troop of Syrians—
Kurds, Turks, and Bedouins, about six hundred horsemen—fell upon
the region of Erbil,
and they plundered and killed a multitude of Christian men from the village of Amkabad and from Surhegan and other villages.
And Baha al-Din, the Kurdish emir, went out from Erbil and engaged them,
and he was broken before them,
and he fled and entered the city.
And those accursed men took great spoil,
women, daughters, and many possessions,
and departed.
And in those days other raiding troops came to the region of Tur Abdin,
and they carried out a great slaughter in the village of Kilshet, and in Bet Man'im, and in its villages (or: Bet Svirina),
and they took much spoil from the region of Bet Rishe and departed.
And in the year 1507 (of the Greeks, 1196 AD),
seventeen days into the month of Haziran (June),
brigands gathered together—Kurds, Turkmens, and Arabs, about four thousand horsemen.
And some say
that three hundred horsemen from the elite Egyptian Mamluks joined them.
And they set their face toward the region of Mosul.
And when they had plundered the villages along their way,
they attacked the city on the morning of Monday the 22nd
in the third month of the Arabs, the year six hundred and eighty-five (AH 685).
